data.content_ref: inline:SRC_001 treats the mechanistic requirement as a legitimate bar the critics fail to meet, but under the audit problem's own framing §11.3 flags are only sustained if they fire as TRUE positives. SRC_001's reasoning that critics operating on a non-mechanistic epistemic register (honesty evaluation, threshold-crossing) cannot produce a causal mechanism is precisely an argument that the mechanistic requirement does not apply to these critics. If the requirement is inapplicable to non-explanatory, evaluative critics, then flagging them for lacking a causal mechanism is a false positive — the flag is firing on a design mismatch, not a genuine deficiency. SRC_001 reclassifies a design mismatch as a true positive without justifying why the ritual's mechanistic bar should apply to evaluative critics at all. The proposed 'fix' (exempt non-mechanistic critics) concedes the bar is inappropriate for them, which means the flag firing on them is not correctly identifying a fault in the critics — it is identifying a misapplied standard.
